claim_being_audited: That rejecting the vendor was compliant because the admissible due-diligence record showed a material unresolved risk at the time of decision, even without proof of a confirmed control failure.
specific_concerns: The available record is only the actor's summary, not the underlying evidence, so the materiality judgment cannot be independently verified.

The policy requires admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk; the summary shows questionnaire/control inconsistency and process gaps, but does not clearly establish why those rose to reject-level materiality.
The policy text says quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies justify follow-up or escalation, but do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
The actor appropriately avoids claiming a confirmed control failure, but the packet still appears to lean on indicators that may support delay or escalation more clearly than outright rejection.
The prior performance issue described is minor and appears weak as support for a reject decision.
unsupported_claims: That the storage-control inconsistency was definitively material enough to justify rejection rather than follow-up or conditional escalation.
That the informal, undocumented quality process independently supported rejection under the stated policy threshold.
That the combined evidence clearly satisfied the policy threshold for 'material unresolved risk' rather than merely leaving diligence incomplete.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying text for BPROC-011-B through BPROC-011-E, especially the exact storage-control inconsistency and whether it was unresolved at decision time.
Provide the formal approval standard or rubric showing what qualifies as a material unresolved risk for vendor rejection.
Provide the procurement analyst's logged recommendation in full, including whether it recommended rejection, hold, or follow-up before approval.
Provide any admissible log showing that the storage-control issue remained unresolved when the rejection was made.
Provide the prior performance record from BPROC-011-A so its severity and relevance can be assessed.
decision_criteria: Reject-level compliance requires admissible due-diligence evidence of a material unresolved risk.
Evidence that only supports follow-up or escalation is insufficient for a clean compliance finding on rejection.
Private or unlogged security-review results cannot be relied on.
Actor framing cannot substitute for the underlying record; materiality must be evidenced, not inferred from tone.
Where the record is narrow and the actor labels support as weak, unresolved policy predicates weigh against a compliant verdict.
